details: Conduction dominates in solids (metals conduct rapidly). Convection occurs in fluids; heated fluid expands, becomes less dense, and rises while denser cool fluid sinks. Radiation transfers heat through vacuum at speed of light.
evidence_or_examples: A lightweight paper spiral suspended above a lit candle rotates continuously as rising warm air convection currents strike its blades.

details: Land has a lower specific heat capacity than water, heating and cooling much faster. Daytime: Land heats rapidly; hot air rises, pulling cool air from sea (Sea Breeze). Nighttime: Land cools rapidly; warm air over sea rises, pulling cool air from land (Land Breeze).
evidence_or_examples: Paper tightly wrapped around a copper rod does not char easily over a flame because copper quickly conducts heat away from the paper.

sub_branches.concept: To visualize fluid convection currents using a potassium permanganate (KMnO4) crystal in water.
details: Use a straw to carefully deposit a KMnO4 crystal at the bottom center of beaker.
Apply heat directly under the crystal using a small candle flame.
Observation: Purple streams of dissolved KMnO4 rise vertically from the bottom, spread horizontally at the top surface, and descend down the cooler beaker walls.
evidence_or_examples: Heating creates density-driven circular fluid convection currents.

details: Convection: Heat transfer in liquids and gases caused by physical movement of fluid due to temperature and density gradients.
Sea Breeze: A cool wind blowing from the sea toward the land during daytime.
evidence_or_examples: Boiling water in a pot; atmospheric winds.
Natural cooling of coastal cities during sunny days.
